text:
Ravi (AP): Heads-up  SinguTech Pte Ltd charged Singapore GST (8%) on our SaaS invoice ST-2026-04 even though we marked the purchase as exported/cloud service to a non-resident. Can tax please confirm whether GST should apply?
Aisha (Finance): Do we have any Singapore GST registration on file? I don't think Redwood is GST-registered in SG. If the supply is considered exported B2B digital services to a non-resident business, IRAS typically zero-rates exports, but vendor must apply the correct treatment.
SinguTech (VendorBot): Uploaded invoice ST-2026-04.pdf (net SGD 10,000; GST SGD 800). Vendor GST Reg: 201912345K. Billing contact says portal defaulted to charge GST.
Ilya (Tax): Quick take: If the customer is a non-resident and the place of supply is outside Singapore, the vendor should not charge GST if it qualifies as an exported service. However, IRAS rules depend on where the service is *consumed* and the contract terms. We need: (1) confirmation of Redwood's business status (non-resident or local GST-registered), (2) statement from vendor acknowledging error, and (3) corrective credit note + replacement invoice showing GST 0% or "exported services - zero-rated".
Ravi (AP): Payment is due tomorrow; holding for now.
Aisha (Finance): Suggested message to vendor (paste/send):
```
Hi <SinguTech AP>,

We are a non-Singapore resident business (Redwood Inference, registered in US/IE). Please can you: (1) issue a credit note canceling the GST amount on ST-2026-04; (2) reissue a replacement invoice with GST 0% and the note "Export of services - zero rated under IRAS guidelines" quoting your GST Reg No 201912345K and our company details; and (3) confirm you will not remit the GST to IRAS for this supply. Also please retain documentary evidence that the service was supplied to a non-resident business (our company registration and invoice references).

Once we receive the CN + replacement invoice we'll release payment.

Thanks,
Aisha, Redwood Finance
```
SinguTech (VendorBot): Vendor reply: "Sorry, our billing stack applied GST by default. We'll issue CN and replacement invoice by EOD and confirm retention of export evidence."
Marta (Legal): Quick note: request they include the customer's company registration number and a line stating "Supply to non-resident business - zero-rated" so we have clear trail for IRAS audit.
Ilya (Tax): Also ask them to confirm the date range the zero-rating applies to (in case their portal misclassified recurring invoices). We'll update vendor master to flag them for exported-service handling.
EngBillingBot: Ticket TAX-599 created to add validation: if customer country != SG then vendor billing should default to zero-rate exported services for supported vendors; assignee = Ravi; due 2026-08-01.
Ravi (AP): CN + replacement uploaded: ST-2026-04-CN.pdf and ST-2026-04-RC.pdf. Replacement shows GST 0% and note: "Export of services - zero rated" and includes both company numbers.
Aisha (Finance): Received. I'll attach docs to vendor file, create CM-2026-33 to clear GST line, and release payment tomorrow. I'll also log this under vendor tax exceptions and notify VendorOps to correct billing profile.
Ilya (Tax): I'll file the exchange in our tax folder for IRAS audit trail. Closing when CM posts.
Ravi (AP): Payment scheduled on corrected invoice tomorrow. Thanks.
